meta.title: dsh-plugin-workspace-browser
meta.description: Open an isolated Chromium window for a DSH workspace.

sessionWorkspaceMissing: This session is not in a registered workspace.
rootAccountDescription: When DSH runs as root, Chromium runs as this existing non-root Linux account. Saving a name does not grant workspace access.
rootAccountMissing: No Linux browser account is configured. In the workspace browser plugin settings, save an existing non-root account under Linux browser account, then check the environment.
rootAccountInvalid: The configured Linux browser account is not usable. In the workspace browser plugin settings, correct the local non-root account name, then check the environment.
rootAccountNameInvalid: Enter the local non-root account name: up to 32 characters, starting with a lowercase letter or underscore, containing only lowercase letters, digits, underscores and hyphens.
workspaceAclToolsMissing: Install the Linux acl package to grant access here. It is not needed if the account already has workspace access.
workspaceGrantRequired: The browser account needs access to the workspace directory.
workspaceAccessUnavailable: Cannot grant access here. Check the ACL tools and directory, or ask your system administrator.
workspaceAccessStale: This confirmation is no longer current. Retry the browser to request a new confirmation.
workspaceAccessBusy: Another workspace access request is in progress. Retry when it finishes.
workspaceAccessFailed: Workspace access could not be verified. Check directory permissions before retrying.
grantRisk: This persistent permission lets this account create, delete, and rename entries directly inside this directory, even after Chromium closes. It is not recursive and does not change permissions on existing files or subdirectories.
clipboardManualHint: For manual copy or paste, open Chromium controls → Transfer clipboard text.
clipboardSelect: Select the Chromium text and copy it using your device’s Copy command.
clipboardInvalid: Use plain text up to 16 KiB.
dockerCliMissing: Docker was not found. Install Docker or check the configured executable.
dockerCliUnavailable: The Docker CLI could not run. Check the configured executable and its permissions.
dockerEndpointUnsupported: This plugin supports only the default local Docker connection.
dockerIdentityUnsupported: On Linux, use a local rootful Docker engine without user namespace remapping. On Windows or macOS, use local Docker Desktop.
runnerWorkspaceInvalid: Check that the registered workspace still names its original directory and that Docker can share it with read/write access.
runnerWorkspacePermissionDenied: The browser cannot read or write the mounted workspace. Check its directory permissions and ACLs.
dockerEngineUnavailable: Could not reach the local Docker engine. Make sure Docker is running.
dockerEngineIncompatible: The workspace browser requires a local Linux/amd64 or Linux/arm64 Docker engine.
runnerImageMissing: The Chromium runner image is missing. Build it in the plugin’s Environment settings.
runnerImageIncompatible: The Chromium runner image is incompatible. Rebuild it in the plugin’s Environment settings.
runnerBuildInputsMissing: The Chromium runner build files are missing or unreadable. Reinstall the complete plugin bundle.
runnerBuildFailed: Docker could not build the Chromium runner image.
runnerBuildTimeout: Building the Chromium runner image timed out.
runnerBuildImageInvalid: The built Chromium runner image did not pass validation.
environmentBuildHelp: Docker builds the Chromium runner image locally. It may download a base image and packages, and can take several minutes.
environmentBuildStatusError: Could not get the runner image build status.
environmentBuildRequestError: Could not request a runner image build.
runnerBundleInvalid: The Chromium image is missing or damaged.
runnerImageLoadFailed: Could not import the Chromium image.
runnerProfileInUse: Another container is using this browser profile.
runnerProfileRecoveryFailed: Could not clear stale Chromium profile locks.
runnerDisplayFailed: The Chromium display could not start.
localDshRequired: This DSH origin is not allowed to access the workspace browser.
handshakeFailed: The browser display could not connect.
handshakeTimeout: The browser display did not connect in time.
requestFailed: The browser service could not complete the request.
sessionAgentAccess: Allow agent browser access for this session
agentAccessDenied: Agent browser access is unavailable. Check the plugin settings and this session’s authorization.
browserNotReady: The browser is not ready. Try again after it starts.
originDescription: Enter one trusted HTTP(S) origin per line, for example https://dsh.example.com. Include any non-default port, but no path or wildcard. Leave empty for local access only. Changes apply without restarting the plugin. Removing your current origin blocks new requests and connections from it; existing display streams stay open.
idleDescription: Stop Chromium after the last workspace view has been disconnected for this long. Changes apply without restarting Chromium. Set to 0 to disable idle shutdown.
idleInvalid: Enter a whole number from 0 to 1440.
agentSettingsLabel: Allow agents to use the workspace browser
agentSettingsDescription: Applies to the current DSH profile. Each session still needs its own authorization. Authorized agents can visit HTTP(S) services on the DSH Host and its private network. Turning this off revokes existing authorizations without interrupting manual browsing.
